summary: You take the Urban Studies core, ECON 1, three skills courses of 3+ units, a community-engaged learning experience, one pathway of at least 20 units (or a self-designed one approved by hand), and the two capstone seminars (10 units, also the WIM), with more URBANST courses numbered 100 and above making up 75 units. Every course needs a letter grade of C or better, except ECON 1 (CR allowed) and Urban Studies courses offered only S/NC, at most 5 units of Directed Reading count, and at most 7 units of internship credit (URBANST 194 and 201A) count. A community-engaged course must carry at least 3 units. The Community-Engaged Scholars Program seminar, the Senior Honors Thesis and prerequisites of your other courses do not count toward the 75 units. Honors adds 5 to 10 units of URBANST 199 and Honors Thesis Support I and II (URBANST 198A, 198B); research or Cardinal Service for community-engaged learning, transfer courses, prerequisites and honors admission, GPA and thesis are checked by hand.

program.why: Grading: "Courses counted toward the 75-unit graduation requirement for the major must be taken for a letter grade, and a minimum grade of C is required. Exceptions are Urban Studies courses numbered 100 and higher offered only on an S/NC basis ... ECON1 may be taken for CR/NC." Letter grades are set on each rule except the Principles of Economics prerequisite, which may be CR/NC. The Bulletin's minimum is 75 units, matching this sentence and the electives text ("If units in the above categories total less than 75"); the self-designed and honors texts say 70.

RxUXAVha-text.why: "The Urban Studies major requires students to complete five types of courses totaling at least 75 units: 24 units in the core (including 5 units for ECON1) / 9 units (minimum) of skills courses in at least three courses of three units each / 20 units (minimum) in an area of concentration / 3 units (minimum) of an internship or Cardinal service-learning course approved by Urban Studies / 10 units in the capstone sequence". Each is its own rule; the 3-unit floor is now on the community-engaged course path. "course , Community-Engaged Scholars Program, course Senior Honors Thesis, and prerequisites for required courses and electives also do not count towards the 75-unit minimum" is a program total for URBANST 196 and 199; other courses' prerequisites have no list and are checked by hand. The rest is advice (calculus, statistics, overseas study).
